answers.answer: For 2 players, deal 4 Player cards each; for 3, deal 3 each; for 4, deal 2 each. Remove the Epidemic cards and set them aside before shuffling and dealing the remaining City and Event cards. Each player's pawn starts in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: remove Epidemic cards; starting hands are 4/3/2 for 2/3/4 players; matching colored pawns in Atlanta.

answers.answer: Place the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2 space. Flip 3 Infection cards and place 3 matching cubes in each named city; flip 3 more and place 2 cubes in each; flip 3 more and place 1 cube in each. Put all 9 revealed cards face up on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: leftmost ‘2’; groups of three receive 3, 2, then 1 cubes; 9 cards to Infection Discard Pile, remainder Infection Deck.

answers.answer: Choose 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic, and remove unused Epidemic cards from the game. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible; shuffle one Epidemic into each pile; stack the piles to form the Player Deck, with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: 4/5/6 difficulty counts; unused Epidemics removed; equal-sized-as-possible piles, one Epidemic in each, smaller piles on bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions, repeating actions if desired and stopping early if desired. Any cards discarded to pay action costs go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve any Epidemics first, and discard or play Events until within the 7-card limit; then Infect Cities by flipping cards equal to the current infection rate. After all three phases, play passes to the left. The active player decides what to do; teammates may offer advice.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: up to 4 actions, repeat/stop; three phases in order; discarded action cards go to Player Discard Pile; turn passes left and active player decides.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry: spend one action to move to a city connected by a white line; no card cost. Direct Flight: discard the City card naming the destination to move there. Charter Flight: discard the City card matching your current city to move to any city. Shuttle Flight: from a city with a research station, move to any other city with a research station. White lines that go off one edge of the board wrap to the other edge (for example, Sydney and Los Angeles are connected).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules: white lines wrap to the other edge.

answers.answer: Normally, spend an action, discard the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it in your current city. If all 6 stations are already built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than 6, set the extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Build a Research Station: discard matching current-city card, take from supply and place; if all 6 built, relocate; extras set aside during setup.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen cured color in that city, returning them to the cube supply. It does not clear the other cured color or the uncured color; each different color requires a separate action. Removed cubes return to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: if cured, return all cubes of that one color from your city; treat each different color with a separate action; cubes return to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 for the Scientist); the station city's color need not match. Move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator. Existing cubes remain, and the disease can still receive cubes from infections and Epidemics until eradicated. If no cubes of that color are on the board when the cure is discovered, immediately eradicate it and flip its marker.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: any station; 5 same-color cards (4 Scientist); existing cubes remain; if no cubes are on board, immediately eradicate and flip marker.

answers.answer: Either give another player the City card matching the city you are both in, or take that matching City card from the other player. Both players must be in that same city and agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card until within the limit.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge: give or take the card matching your current city; same city; both agree; recipient exceeding 7 immediately discards or plays an Event.

answers.answer: When sharing, the Researcher may give any City card from the Researcher's hand to a player in the same city, not only the matching city card. This may happen on either player's turn. The exception only allows a transfer from the Researcher to the other player; the other player may not use it to give the Researcher an arbitrary nonmatching City card.
answers.evidence: Roles, Researcher: may give any City card to a player in same city; only transfers from Researcher's hand, on either player's turn; no reverse arbitrary transfer.

answers.answer: After actions, draw the top 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends and players lose; discards are not reshuffled. If Epidemics are drawn, resolve them first, then discard or play Events until within the 7-card limit.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: draw top 2 together; fewer than 2 means loss, do not reshuffle discards. Hand Limit: first resolve Epidemics, then reduce hand.

answers.answer: Resolve the Epidemic in order: (1) increase the Infection Rate marker by 1 space; (2) draw the bottom Infection card, place 3 matching cubes in its city unless eradicated; since that city has 2 cubes, add only enough to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs; discard this Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile; (3) reshuffle only the Infection Discard Pile and place it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game afterward; do not draw a replacement Player card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: three ordered steps; at 2 existing cubes, add to 3 then outbreak; Infection card to Infection Discard Pile; Intensify only that pile onto deck; no replacement.

answers.answer: The number of Infection cards flipped after 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics is respectively 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4.
answers.evidence: Player Reference, Infection Rate Track: Epidemics resolved 0–6 map to 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4 cards.

answers.answer: Resolve the first Epidemic completely, including Increase, Infect, and Intensify, then resolve all three steps of the second. Events may be played between the two Epidemics. After resolving Epidemics drawn, reduce any over-limit hand by discarding cards or playing Events until at most 7; drawn Epidemics take priority and are not replaced.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: two drawn together resolve all steps for first, then second; Events may be played between. Hand Limit: first resolve Epidemics, then reduce hand.

answers.answer: Flip Infection cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For a non-eradicated disease, place 1 matching cube in the named city; if it already has 3 of that color, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. For an eradicated disease, place no cube. A cured but not eradicated disease still gets the normal placement and can cause an outbreak. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of deck, current-rate count; one cube unless eradicated; 3 cubes causes outbreak instead of fourth; each card to discard. Cure Procedure says cured disease still infects until eradication.

answers.answer: When the first outbreak occurs, move the Outbreaks marker forward 1 space, then place 1 cube of that color on every connected city. If a connected city already has 3 cubes of that color, it has a chain-reaction outbreak after the current outbreak resolves, and the marker moves forward 1 more space for that outbreak. During the chain reaction, do not add cubes to cities that already had an outbreak while resolving this Infection card, so it does not spread back into the first city if that city already had its outbreak. Each color can have up to 3 cubes in a city; different colors have separate caps.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker +1, spread to every connected city, chain reactions after current outbreak resolves; skip adding cubes to cities already outbroken on this card; up to 3 of each color.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played after the Infection card is drawn but before resolving its outbreak, because Events cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card. After resolving the current Infection card, an Event may be played before drawing the next Infection card. Any player may play Airlift at any time when not between a card draw and its resolution; the player who plays it chooses its use. It costs no action, moves one pawn to any city, and requires permission for another player's pawn. Discard the Event to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any player, any time, not between drawing and resolving a card; player who plays decides use; Airlift moves pawn to any city; played Events to Player Discard Pile. Events are not actions.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes 1 Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Contingency Planner Role card. The storage limit is 1, and it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove that Event from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Roles, Contingency Planner: action; Event from anywhere in Player Discard Pile; store one on role card, outside hand limit; remove from game when played.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own; moving another player's pawn requires the owner's agreement. Direct/Charter Flight discards come from the Dispatcher's hand. For a Charter Flight, the card must match the moved pawn's departure city, not the Dispatcher's location. The Dispatcher may move another pawn but cannot make it Treat Disease or take other nonmovement actions. The Dispatcher cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Roles, Dispatcher: both movement options and owner agreement; cards from Dispatcher's hand, Charter matches moved pawn's departure; cannot direct nonmovement actions or use Operations Expert move.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; eradication and a clear board are not required. They lose if the Outbreaks marker reaches its last space (8th outbreak), if they cannot place the required disease cubes of a needed color (during Epidemics, outbreaks, or infections), or if a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after actions. Insufficient cube supply causes an immediate loss when the required placement is attempted.
answers.evidence: Victory: cures for all 4; eradication not needed. Defeat lists 8th outbreak, insufficient cube supply, and inability to draw 2; Cube supply check says immediate loss.

answers.answer: Place the board within reach; put the 6 research stations and separated disease cubes nearby. Place 1 research station in Atlanta, the Outbreaks marker on 0, and the 4 Cure markers vial-side up near the Discovered Cure Indicators. Give each player a Reference card. Shuffle Role cards and deal 1 face up to each player; place matching pawns in Atlanta and remove unused Role cards and pawns. The player with the highest-population City card goes first.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 9: board and supplies, Atlanta station, markers, Reference and Role card dealing, pawns, unused roles/pawns removed; highest-population City card starts.

answers.answer: The player whose turn it is decides what to do; teammates may freely offer advice. In an Introductory game, play with cards face up for all to see. In Standard/Heroic, hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may examine either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: active player decides. Special Rules: Introductory open cards; Standard/Heroic private by default, experienced groups may open; anyone may examine either discard pile.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube of an uncured disease does not eradicate it and has no effect. If the last cube of a cured disease is removed, it becomes eradicated and its Cure marker is flipped to the eradication side. Eradicated diseases receive no new cubes during normal infections or Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Eradication: last cube of cured disease triggers eradication and marker flip; last cube of uncured disease has no effect; eradicated diseases get no new cubes in infections or Epidemics.

answers.answer: The Epidemic Infect step places 3 cubes of the matching color in the unprotected city because it starts with zero cubes. There is no outbreak simply for placing the city at 3; the summary says the outbreak occurs when the city already has cubes of that color. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Infect: place 3 cubes; outbreak clause is for a city that already has cubes; discard card to Infection Discard Pile, then Intensify.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. The bottom Infection card is drawn, but no cubes are placed because the disease is eradicated. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile, then Intensify by reshuffling only that discard pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic steps: Increase; Infect bottom card and place cubes unless eradicated; discard card; Intensify only Infection Discard Pile onto deck.

answers.answer: After the first Epidemic's Intensify, the Infection Discard Pile is empty. The second bottom Infection card is therefore the only card shuffled during the second Intensify, and it ends up on top of the Infection Deck. On the immediately following normal Infection step, that city is drawn first; it is brought to 3 matching cubes by the second Epidemic, and the normal infection causes an outbreak because it already has 3, unless an Event, eradication, or role protection prevents it.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once: second bottom card is only card in second Intensify and ends on top; second Epidemic brings city to 3; drawn first in normal infections and causes outbreak subject to listed prevention.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs only 4 City cards of the same color instead of 5 to Discover a Cure. The action still requires being at any research station, and the cards still must match the disease color; the station city's color need not match.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: 4 for Scientist, at any research station, 5 cards of disease color; station city color need not match. Scientist role repeats 4-card requirement.

answers.answer: As an action, the Operations Expert builds a research station in the city the Operations Expert currently occupies. No City card is needed, used, or discarded.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert: as an action, build a research station in the current city with no City card needed, used or discarded.

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, the Operations Expert may move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The card does not need to match the destination or departure city.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert: once per turn as an action, move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.

answers.answer: A Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the Medic's city. It does not remove cubes of multiple colors in one action; another color requires another action.
answers.evidence: Medic: Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color. Actions: treat each different color with a separate action.

answers.answer: When the cure is discovered while the Medic is already in a city with cubes of that cured color, remove those cubes there immediately, with no separate Treat Disease action. Later, when another player moves the Medic into another city containing cubes of that cured color via Dispatcher or Airlift, the Medic automatically removes all cubes of that color there upon entering; that movement is performed through the relevant Dispatcher action or Airlift Event, not a separate Medic treatment action.
answers.evidence: Medic role: if already in a city when cure discovered, remove cubes immediately; entering via Dispatcher or Airlift on another player's turn also triggers automatic removal.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the city the Medic occupies. This protection does not extend to adjacent cities and does not apply to uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Medic: prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in Medic's city, but not adjacent cities or uncured diseases.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist prevents placement and outbreaks of every disease color in the Specialist's current city and all cities connected to it. This ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Quarantine Specialist role: every disease color, current and all connected cities; setup cubes unaffected.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any 1 Infection card from the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between an Epidemic's Infect and Intensify steps, so it may remove the Infection card just discarded during that Epidemic before Intensify shuffles the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: remove any 1 card in Infection Discard Pile from game; may play between Infect and Intensify.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, so no Infection cards are flipped for that step. It does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, One Quiet Night: skip next Infect Cities step (do not flip Infection cards); does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any 1 pawn to any city. If it is another player's pawn, get that player's permission. The player who plays the Event chooses how it is used.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Airlift moves any 1 pawn to any city, permission for another player's pawn; Event player decides use.

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the 7-card hand limit; Role and Reference cards do not. A Contingency Planner Event stored on the Role card also does not count. Reduce a hand of 9 by discarding cards or playing Event cards until at most 7; first resolve any Epidemics just drawn, then reduce the hand.
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: 7 Player cards only; Roles and References don't count. Contingency Planner stored card doesn't count; reduce to 7 after resolving Epidemics.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, regardless of the player's location, with no City card discard required.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, Government Grant: place a research station in any city (no card discard needed).

answers.answer: Forecast lets you draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put those cards back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, Forecast: draw, view, rearrange top 6 Infection Deck cards, then put them back on top.
